Potential Logic Issue with Readonly User Setup (Lines 547-549)
Severity: Medium File: gui/gui_test/overview_menu/test_overview_menu.robot Line: 547-549

Issue: The keyword includes logic to create a readonly user, but the test case "Verify Asset Tag Update With Readonly User" already has [Setup] Create Readonly User And Login To GUI in its setup (Line 436). This creates redundant user creation.

Why: Redundant user creation causes several problems:

Performance: Creating users twice unnecessarily slows down test execution
Potential Conflicts: Attempting to create the same user twice may cause errors or unexpected behavior
Maintenance Burden: Two places to update if user creation logic changes
Code Clarity: Unclear which creation is actually needed, confusing for future maintainers
Test Reliability: If the first creation succeeds but second fails (or vice versa), test behavior becomes unpredictable
Best Practice Violation: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle - setup logic should be in one place
Current Code:

    # Setup for readonly user.
    IF  '${user_type}' == 'readonly'
       Create Readonly User And Login To GUI
    END

Recommendation: Remove the redundant user creation from the keyword since it's already handled in the test case setup:

    # Note: Readonly user setup is handled by test case [Setup] when needed
Or alternatively, remove the [Setup] from the test case and rely solely on the keyword's logic.

Potential Race Condition (Line 552)
Severity: Low File: gui/gui_test/overview_menu/test_overview_menu.robot Line: 552

Issue: Using Wait AND Click Element without verifying the element is clickable could lead to flaky tests.

Why: Waiting only for element visibility doesn't guarantee clickability, which can cause:

Flaky Tests: Element might be visible but disabled, covered by another element, or still animating
False Failures: Tests fail intermittently in CI/CD pipelines due to timing issues
Debugging Difficulty: Race conditions are hard to reproduce and diagnose
CI/CD Instability: Flaky tests reduce confidence in the test suite and slow down development
Best Practice: Selenium/Robot Framework best practices recommend explicit wait for clickability
Real-World Scenarios:
Button might be visible but disabled during page load
Modal overlays or loading spinners might cover the button
CSS animations might make button temporarily unclickable


Current Code:

    Wait AND Click Element  ${xpath_asset_tag_edit_button}


Recommendation: Add explicit wait for element to be clickable:

    Wait Until Element Is Enabled  ${xpath_asset_tag_edit_button}  timeout=10
    Click Element  ${xpath_asset_tag_edit_button}

Wait AND Click Element  ${xpath_asset_tag_edit_button} doing same .
Wait And Click Element
    [Documentation]  Wait until element is visible then click the element.
    [Arguments]  ${locator}  ${wait_timeout}=10s

    # Description of argument(s):
    # locator        xpath of the element.
    # wait_timeout   timeout for the locator to visible.

    Wait Until Element Is Visible    ${locator}    timeout=${wait_timeout}
    Click Element    ${locator}

Variable Naming Inconsistency and Deprecated Keyword (Lines 555-556)
Severity: Medium File: gui/gui_test/overview_menu/test_overview_menu.robot Line: 555-556

Issue: Two problems: (1) The variable ${new_hostname} is misleading because it's being used for asset tag, not hostname. (2) Using deprecated Set Variable keyword instead of modern VAR syntax.

Why:

Misleading variable names cause significant problems:

Confusion: Developers reading the code will expect hostname operations, not asset tag operations
Maintenance Errors: Future changes to hostname logic might accidentally modify asset tag logic (or vice versa)
Debugging Difficulty: When tests fail, misleading names make it harder to identify the actual problem
Copy-Paste Errors: This suggests the code was copied from hostname-related tests without proper adaptation
Semantic Mismatch: The test is about asset tags, but variables reference hostname - creates cognitive dissonance
Using deprecated Set Variable is problematic:

Set Variable is deprecated since Robot Framework 7.0 (Robocop: DEPR05)
Modern VAR syntax is more concise, readable, and maintainable
Deprecated keywords will eventually be removed from Robot Framework
Using deprecated syntax makes code harder to maintain and update
VAR syntax is the recommended approach in all new code
Current Code:

    ${overview_hostname}=  Get Text  ${xpath_hostname}
    ${new_hostname}=  Set Variable  ${overview_hostname}_new
    
Recommendation: Use accurate variable names AND modern VAR syntax:

    ${current_asset_tag}=  Get Text  ${xpath_hostname}
    VAR    ${new_asset_tag}    ${current_asset_tag}_new

Inconsistent Indentation in IF Block (Lines 562-570)
Severity: Medium File: gui/gui_test/overview_menu/test_overview_menu.robot Line: 562-570

Issue: The indentation inside the nested IF blocks is inconsistent. Line 560 has incorrect indentation.

Why: Consistent indentation is critical in Robot Framework because:

It defines the logical structure and scope of control flow statements
Inconsistent indentation makes code harder to read and maintain
It can lead to confusion about which statements belong to which block
Robot Framework style guide recommends 4 spaces per indentation level
Mixed indentation (6 spaces vs 7 spaces) suggests copy-paste errors or manual editing mistakes
Automated tools (robocop, robot.tidy) will flag this as a style violation

Current Code:

    IF  '${action}' == 'save'
      Click Element  ${xpath_asset_tag_save_button}
       IF  '${user_type}' == 'readonly'
          Verify Error And Unauthorized Message On GUI
       ELSE
          Verify Success Message On BMC GUI Page
       END
       Page Should Not Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag_save_button}
       Element Should Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag} ${new_hostname}

Problem: Line 563 uses 6 spaces, while lines 564-570 use 7 spaces. This creates inconsistent indentation levels.

Recommendation: Use consistent indentation (4 spaces per level):

    IF  '${action}' == 'save'
        Click Element  ${xpath_asset_tag_save_button}
        IF  '${user_type}' == 'readonly'
            Verify Error And Unauthorized Message On GUI
        ELSE
            Verify Success Message On BMC GUI Page
        END
        Page Should Not Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag_save_button}
        Element Should Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag}  ${new_hostname}

2. Incorrect Variable Reference in Assertion (Line 570)
Severity: High File: gui/gui_test/overview_menu/test_overview_menu.robot Line: 570

Issue: Missing space between XPath variable and the expected value in the Element Should Contain assertion. This will cause a syntax error.

Why: Robot Framework requires at least two spaces (or a tab) to separate arguments. With only one space, Robot Framework will interpret ${xpath_asset_tag} ${new_hostname} as a single concatenated string argument instead of two separate arguments. The Element Should Contain keyword expects exactly 2 arguments (locator and expected text), so this will cause:

Runtime error: "Keyword 'Element Should Contain' expected 2 arguments, got 1"
Test execution failure
Incorrect validation logic

Current Code:

       Element Should Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag} ${new_hostname}

Problem: There's only one space between ${xpath_asset_tag} and ${new_hostname}, which violates Robot Framework's argument separation rules.

Recommendation: Add proper spacing or use separate arguments:

       Element Should Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag}  ${new_hostname}

Missing Validation After Cancel Action (Lines 571-573)
Severity: Low File: gui/gui_test/overview_menu/test_overview_menu.robot Line: 571-573

Issue: The ELSE block (cancel action) only verifies the cancel button disappears but doesn't verify that the asset tag value was NOT changed.

Why: Incomplete validation creates a weak test that might miss bugs:

Incomplete Test Coverage: The test doesn't verify the primary purpose of the Cancel button (discarding changes)
False Confidence: Test passes even if Cancel button saves changes instead of discarding them
Regression Risk: Future code changes could break Cancel functionality without test detection
Test Purpose Mismatch: Test documentation says "verify that asset tag update is discarded" but code doesn't verify this
Real Bug Scenario: If Cancel button has a bug and saves changes anyway, this test would still pass
Best Practice: Every test should verify both positive outcomes (what should happen) and negative outcomes (what should NOT happen)

Current Code:

   ELSE
      Click Element  ${xpath_asset_tag_cancel_button}
      Page Should Not Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag_cancel_button}
    END
    
    
Recommendation: Add validation that the original value is preserved:

   ELSE
      Click Element  ${xpath_asset_tag_cancel_button}
      Page Should Not Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag_cancel_button}
      Element Should Contain  ${xpath_asset_tag}  ${overview_hostname}
    END
